doc.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Gil as mentor and the memorial concert at St. Peter's
summary: Levin calls Gil a mentor to many, and recalls the packed memorial concert for him.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: He was absolutely incredible. It was like going to music school but it was way beyond that. He was like a mentor and a teacher to so many people. And a lot of people went through that band in the 70s and 80s and I’m sure they would tell you the same thing that their playing and their musical thinking is affected by the time they spent with Gil. And anybody that they’ve worked with, I mean it just kind of spreads. I mentioned the memorial concert for Manny Albam. There was one for Gil at St. Peter’s in the 80s after he had passed. And the place was packed like beyond its capability to handle people. It wasn’t just standing room only, it was standing room like this in the balconies and the entrances, and people had flown over from England and Europe just to go to that and then went right back. They were just kind of looking around the room and realized how many people he had affected. And those were just the people who could get there that day.
